content: Pre-trained representations mostly impacts the training time of the sequence to sequence model (see Appendix SECREF7 ): slows throughput during training by about 5.3x and is even slower because of the need to backpropagate through the LM for fine-tuning (9.2x). However, inference is only 12-14% slower than the baseline when adding pre-trained embeddings to the encoder (, ). This is because the LM computation can be paralelized for all input tokens. Inference is much slower when adding representations to the decoder because the LM needs to be invoked repeatedly. Our current implementation does not cache LM operations for the previous state and can be made much faster.
